about: Native rewrites for skills that read chat history or author skills, the help and teaching skills, the principles, and the bundled cursor-team-kit skills. See docs/claude-code-mapping.md.

edits.find: Never edit a skill under `plugins/cache/`. Before approval, show its destination, `.cursor/skills/<skill>/` or `~/.cursor/skills/<skill>/`. After approval, copy the skill folder there and edit the copy. Never open a PR or push.
edits.replace: Never edit a skill under `plugins/cache/`, and never copy a plugin skill to `.claude/skills/` or `~/.claude/skills/` to edit it. The copy only adds its own `/<skill>` command. `/<plugin>:<skill>` and every skill that reads the plugin skill by path still run the plugin's text. Put each approved edit to a plugin skill in a rule file instead, `.claude/rules/<plugin>-<skill>.md` for this project or `~/.claude/rules/<plugin>-<skill>.md` for every project, such as `~/.claude/rules/omc-pstack-fy-reflect.md` for `/omc-pstack-fy:reflect`. Open the rule with its condition, such as "When you run the omc-pstack-fy `reflect` skill,", so it does nothing otherwise. A rule cannot delete the plugin's text, so when an edit changes or removes a step, quote that step in the rule and say the rule replaces it. Write the plugin's version beside each edit, from the `version` in its `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` or the version folder in its cache path, or the date when it has neither, because a later release can make the edit stale. Add to the file when it exists. Before approval, show each edit's rule file path. After you write it, say that a new or changed rule file takes effect in the next session. Never open a PR or push.
edits.why: Claude Code loads a plugin skill and a same-named skill in `.claude/skills/` or `~/.claude/skills/` side by side, because plugin skills are namespaced as `/plugin-name:skill-name`, so an edited copy never replaces the plugin's text. A rule file without `paths` loads at launch, so a new or changed rule takes effect in the next session. Subagents load it too, except Explore, Plan, and subagents that set `omitClaudeMd`. So the edit reaches the slash command, skills that read the skill by path, and most delegates. Leaving `project` out of `--setting-sources` skips project rules, and the `managed-only` Project instructions setting skips `.claude/rules/` files. A rule cannot delete plugin text, and Claude may pick either of two instructions that contradict, so a rule that changes or removes a step quotes that step and says the rule replaces it. The file lives outside the plugin cache, so by construction a plugin update leaves it in place. For the same reason a later release can make it stale, so each edit records the plugin version.

edits.find: A skill that should have fired gets its description tuned.
edits.replace: A skill that should have fired gets its description tuned, unless it is a plugin skill. A plugin skill runs as `/<plugin>:<skill>`, where `<plugin>` is the `name` in its plugin's `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, and its files usually sit under `~/.claude/plugins/cache/`. Its edits go to a rule file, which cannot change a description, so that finding goes to the backlog.
edits.why: Claude Code namespaces every plugin skill as `/plugin-name:skill-name`, and a plugin loaded with `--plugin-dir` sits outside `plugins/cache/`, so the path alone does not identify a plugin skill. A colon in the command does not identify one either, because a nested project skill and a skill from `--add-dir` also run as `/<x>:<y>`. So the definition names the plugin's manifest. A plugin skill's edits go to a rule file, which cannot change the skill's frontmatter description.

edits.find: Locate the active workspace's transcripts before fanning out. The system prompt names the workspace's `agent-transcripts/` directory. Use only that path. Don't glob across `~/.cursor/projects/*/`. That crosses workspace boundaries and reads private chats from unrelated projects.
edits.replace: Locate the active workspace's transcripts before fanning out. They live in `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/`, one `<session>.jsonl` per session, where the slug is the workspace path with every character that is not a letter or digit changed to `-`. Use only that folder. Don't glob across `~/.claude/projects/*/`. That crosses workspace boundaries and reads private chats from unrelated projects. The user's own words are the `type: "user"` lines whose `message.content` is a string or `text` blocks, minus `isMeta: true` lines. A `type: "user"` line with `tool_result` blocks is tool output, so it is no evidence of a preference.
edits.why: Claude Code keeps transcripts in ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/, and the system prompt does not name the folder. Tool results share type user with human messages, so miners must tell them apart.

edits.find: Transcripts live at `~/.cursor/projects/<slug>/agent-transcripts/<uuid>/<uuid>.jsonl`, where `<slug>` is the workspace path with the leading slash dropped and each "/" turned into "-" (so `/Users/you/proj` becomes `Users-you-proj`). Every line is one chat message.
edits.replace: Transcripts live at `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<uuid>.jsonl`, one file per session, where `<slug>` is the workspace path with every character that is not a letter or digit turned into "-" (so `/Users/you/my_proj` becomes `-Users-you-my-proj`). A session's subagent transcripts sit in `<uuid>/subagents/`. Every line is one JSON event. The user's messages are `type: "user"` lines whose `message.content` is a string or `text` blocks. Skip `isMeta: true` lines, which hold injected text such as a skill body. A `type: "user"` line with `tool_result` blocks is tool output, not the user. The assistant's words are `text` blocks in `type: "assistant"` lines.
edits.why: Claude Code stores one JSONL file per session under ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/, and its slug keeps the leading dash and replaces every non-alphanumeric character. Lines are events, not messages, so the miners must tell the user's words from tool output.

edits.find: Spawn one investigator subagent per source, in agent mode because readonly strips MCP access, and ask each
edits.replace: Spawn one investigator subagent per source with `subagent_type: "general-purpose"`, because it keeps the session's MCP servers, and ask each
edits.why: Claude Code has no agent mode or readonly mode. Per the `readonly: false` row of docs/claude-code-mapping.md, `general-purpose` keeps the session's MCP servers, which the per-source investigators need.

edits.find: Read this run's transcript under the active workspace's `agent-transcripts/` directory (the system prompt names the path). Don't glob across `~/.cursor/projects/*/`. That reads unrelated private chats.
edits.replace: Read this run's transcript in the active workspace's project folder, `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/`, where the slug is the workspace path with every character that is not a letter or digit changed to `-`. The newest `<session>.jsonl` directly in it is the current session, and its subagents' transcripts are in `<session>/subagents/`. Don't glob across `~/.claude/projects/*/`. That reads unrelated private chats. In the transcript, what the agent did is the `tool_use` blocks in `type: "assistant"` lines. What came back is the `tool_result` blocks in the `type: "user"` lines after them, which are tool output, not the user.
edits.why: Claude Code keeps transcripts in ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/, and the system prompt does not name the folder. The audit checks actions, which live in tool_use and tool_result blocks.

edits.find: Before handing back, spawn a subagent on another vendor's model than the one that did the work. Self-review is not a substitute. The subagent reads the audit trail and the run's transcript, then flags what the user should pay attention to. Not a redo of the work, a scan for what's suboptimal or risky.
edits.replace: Before handing back, get a review from a model other than the one that did the work. Read the `second opinion` line in `~/.claude/rules/omc-pstack-fy-models.md` and pick one entry, on a different vendor from yours when the line offers one, else on a different model. When every entry shares your model, follow the no-line rule below. A Claude entry runs as a subagent. An external entry, such as `gemini:gemini-2.5-pro`, runs read-only through the **pstack-ask** skill. Its throwaway copy of the repository does not reach the transcript or a log kept out of git, so inline the log and a digest of this run's actions in its prompt. With no line, spawn a subagent with `model` set to `sonnet` when the work ran on `opus`, and to `opus` otherwise. Self-review is not a substitute. The reviewer reads the audit trail and the run's transcript, then flags what the user should pay attention to. Not a redo of the work, a scan for what's suboptimal or risky.
edits.why: Upstream asks for another vendor's model. An Agent spawn runs only Claude models, so the `second opinion` line may name another vendor's model through pstack-ask, per the Phase 3 contract. With no line, a different Claude model is the closest match.

edits.find: Lead with the reviewer's model on its own line (`reviewed by <model>`), then list each flag pointing to specific rows or moments.
edits.replace: Lead with the reviewer's model on its own line (`reviewed by <model>`). On the next line, name the panel. "Cross-vendor panel (claude, codex)" is stronger evidence than "same-vendor panel (opus, sonnet)". Then list each flag pointing to specific rows or moments.
edits.why: The reviewer may be another Claude model or another vendor's. Naming the panel, per the Phase 3 contract, tells the user what the review is worth.

edits.find:
pstack is built for Cursor, and it also installs in Claude Code with `/plugin marketplace add cursor/plugins`, then `/plugin install pstack@cursor-plugins`. There, each command takes a `pstack:` prefix, such as `/pstack:poteto-mode`. The [Claude Code adapter](../../docs/harness/claude-code.md) maps the Cursor names, and a step that needs a Cursor-only feature, such as Bugbot or Automations, is skipped with a one-line note.

Other tools can read the skills, because they use the Agent Skills format. But most workflow skills, including `/poteto-mode`, `/how`, and `/teach`, spawn Cursor subagents, some with per-role models, and Custom Modes and `/loop` are Cursor features, so those parts may not work there.
edits.replace:
omc-pstack-fy is a personal Claude Code build of pstack, the Cursor plugin by Lauren Tan. A step that needs a Cursor-only service, such as a webhook routine, is skipped with a one-line note.

Other tools can read the skills, because they use the Agent Skills format. But most workflow skills, including `/poteto-mode`, `/how`, and `/teach`, spawn Claude Code subagents, some with per-role models, and `/loop` is a Claude Code command, so those parts may not work there.
edits.why: The reader runs Claude Code. The skills are native, so the adapter is gone, and install moved to step 1.

edits.find:
Whether `/poteto-mode` stays on depends on how the user starts it:

- Enter on `/poteto-mode` attaches the skill to one message. It fades as the chat moves on.
- Option+Enter on Mac or Alt+Enter on Windows, or Use as Mode from the skill entry, makes it a Custom Mode. It stays in context every turn until the user exits the mode, and it stays out of casual turns.
- Cursor's docs list Custom Modes in the Agents Window and the CLI. Elsewhere, start each new task with `/poteto-mode`.

Link [Cursor's skills docs](https://cursor.com/docs/skills) when this comes up. Mid-chat, "new task" makes the mode match a fresh playbook. `/poteto-mode` already uses `poteto-agent` for the subagents its playbook steps spawn. To get the same style from a subagent of your own, spawn it with `subagent_type: "poteto-agent"`.
edits.replace:
How long `/poteto-mode` stays on:

- Typing `/poteto-mode` loads the skill into the session. It stays in context on every later turn. There is no mode to switch on or off.
- A compaction keeps only the start of a long skill, or drops it, and a new session starts without it. Run `/poteto-mode` again after either one.

Link [Claude Code's skills docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills) when this comes up. Mid-session, "new task" makes the mode match a fresh playbook. `/poteto-mode` already uses `omc-pstack-fy:poteto-agent` for the subagents its playbook steps spawn. To get the same style from a subagent of your own, spawn it with `subagent_type: "omc-pstack-fy:poteto-agent"`.
edits.why: Claude Code has no Custom Mode. Its skills docs say an invoked skill stays in the conversation, and compaction re-attaches only the first 5,000 tokens of each skill within a shared budget. Plugin agents take the plugin prefix.

edits.find:
Not in pstack:

- `/deslop`, `control-cli`, and `control-ui` ship in the `cursor-team-kit` plugin.
- `/loop` and `/create-skill` are Cursor built-ins.
edits.replace:
Bundled with omc-pstack-fy, but not part of pstack:

- `/deslop` cleans AI slop out of the branch diff. `/control-ui` and `/control-cli` drive a web or Electron UI, or a CLI or TUI, to prove a change works. They come from another plugin in the same upstream repository, because `/poteto-mode` and its playbooks call them.

Not in pstack:

- `/loop` is a Claude Code command, and `skill-creator` is a separate skill for authoring skills.
edits.why: omc-pstack-fy bundles deslop, control-ui, and control-cli. Claude Code has its own /loop and no create-skill.
